sources.entry: ChannelTube ⚠ - Download video or audio from YouTube channels on a schedule via yt-dlp. AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: ChannelTube is a Docker-based tool that syncs and downloads video or audio from YouTube channels on a schedule, using yt-dlp.
summary.what_it_does: Runs as a Docker container with a web interface on port 5000 that synchronizes content from YouTube channels using yt-dlp. It fetches new items at hours you set in a comma-separated schedule, with a deadband of up to 10 minutes from the scheduled start. Video and audio go to separate mounted folders. Format IDs, fallback video and audio codecs, thread count, and a short-video cutoff (default 180 seconds) are configurable via environment variables. Subtitles can be none, embedded, or saved externally, for chosen languages. Optional features include nightly yt-dlp auto-updates (stable or nightly builds), including video ID in filenames, and a Plex and/or Jellyfin library scan after new content arrives. A cookies.txt file in the config folder can be used for yt-dlp.
use_cases: Download new videos from YouTube channels automatically
Archive YouTube channel audio as a music or podcast library
Keep a local copy of channel uploads for a media server
Schedule nightly YouTube syncs in a home media setup
Refresh a Plex or Jellyfin library after new YouTube downloads
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yml with the image thewicklowwolf/channeltube:latest, mapping /channeltube/config, /channeltube/downloads, /channeltube/audio_downloads and port 5000
Open the web interface on port 5000 and add YouTube channels
Optionally set environment variables such as PUID, PGID, subtitles, and auto_update_hour
notable: Scheduled sync by hour of day, with separate video and audio download directories
Optional Plex and Jellyfin library scan triggered when new content is retrieved
Configurable yt-dlp format IDs and fallback codecs via environment variables
Subtitle handling with none, embed, or external options and language selection
Cookies file support for yt-dlp via the config folder
caveats: The README does not describe a platform beyond Docker, and does not state limits on channel count or volume
Relies on yt-dlp, so downloads depend on YouTube behaviour and yt-dlp updates
Cookies setup is a manual browser-export process
